quick.topic: Group users by what they came to do
quick.summary: Why splitting by sign up month can show nothing, and segments that explain behaviour.
quick.takeaway: Group people by what they are trying to do.

parts.title: Group users by what they came to do

beats.line: I split users by sign up month. Nothing stood out. Why?

board.text: Group by what they came to do

beats.line: Sign up month rarely changes what people want.
Group them by what they came to do instead.

board.text: group by goal, not by date

beats.line: Some came to compare prices. Some came to buy today.
How do I know what someone came to do?
From what they did first, and from research notes on why.
Then compare how each group moves through the product.
Comparers leave at the price page. Buyers finish fine.
Now the team knows which people to help, and where.

quiz.question: Which grouping is most likely to explain why some users leave?
options: What users came to do, such as compare or buy
Whether they signed up on a weekday
quiz.explanation: Groups based on what people are trying to do often behave differently, which explains the numbers.

quiz.question: Segments based on what users are trying to do often explain behaviour better than sign up dates.
quiz.explanation: What people want shapes what they do, so goal-based groups show clearer differences.
